::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 23d [after 1865]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS University of Iowa; MsL/Y56/23.Nov.
:::

My dear Madam
That poem on the Sabbath Bells was given me by Lady [Lucy Herbert](people/person_679.qmd), [Lord Powis](people/person_2076.qmd)’s sister, at the time when she was collecting subscriptions for [bells for Auckland](organizations/other_103.qmd) Cathedral New Zealand. She sent it to me undoubtingly to be printed with an appeal we were then making. She has since married and I cannot remember her present name - but perhaps you know her, and at any rate her sister, Lady [Harriet Herbert](people/person_680.qmd) would, I am sure, be glad to tell you how the verses came into their family[^1]

yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: William Wordsworth, *Ecclesiastical Sonnets*, 28, begins: 'The Sabbath bells renew the inviting peal', and may be the poem referred to.
